rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at intermediate temperature to maximize the chance of observing all 10 compounds while revealing crowded retention regions. The remaining acquisition time provides a strong-solvent hold for late-eluting compounds.

Double the gradient slope to shorten the run while testing how much of the ample resolution margin is retained. Keep temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Use an intermediate gradient duration to recover resolution of the crowded central peaks while targeting a last-peak time below 10 minutes. This tests whether full resolution and zero time penalty can be achieved together.

The current method is close to the maximum score, with only one pair slightly below R = 1.5. Increase temperature by one grid step to test a selectivity shift while preserving the gradient and potentially shortening retention.

This gives a slightly shallower gradient than injection 3, predicting critical-pair resolution near 1.57 and last-peak elution near 9.9 minutes. All peaks should elute during the gradient, potentially achieving full resolution with no time penalty.

Test whether a steeper gradient can retain the maximum CRF while shortening the run further. Keep temperature fixed at the successful high-temperature condition to isolate the gradient effect.

Flatten injection 12's gradient to recover the limiting central separation while retaining its improved separation of the other close pair. This targets a maximum-score alternative with a larger resolution margin and last-peak elution below 10 minutes.
